note: THE DECLARED SHIPPED SET of the carry family, as DATA. Every row is [D, DV, warps_per_cta] -- the routing depth, the value width and the CTA's warp count -- and that triple is the WHOLE key: the mode word, the stream counts and the park bit are runtime, the window and the chunk are the descriptor's (KERNEL_STANDARDS §R11/§R16). A row in `shipped` is built by a default install; a row in `test` is a conformance arm built for the battery and never shipped. (4, 64, 8) is the row the read-member verdict wants and it is NOT declared: measured on this line its census is 255 registers with 176 bytes of local, and 254/160 with the sparse bodies compiled out -- the depth-four addressing walks and member set exceed the register file at eight warps in the UNION body already, so declaring it would put a spilling arm in the battery. It returns with the register relief (the parked low plane), and the measurement is in the K3 journal. `warps_per_cta` keeps 4 in its DOMAIN while no row names it: one CTA per SM is the design point on every architecture, and the two-CTA latency diagnostic returns only if a measurement asks for it. Rows are canonical-sorted and the generator refuses any other spelling, so an arm's INDEX -- which the selection header, the per-arm translation units and `ROLA_CARRY_ARMS` all name -- is a property of the declaration and not of an editor's insertion point.
